easy.def: Having lived or been here a long time.
examples: My grandpa is old.
The old house is empty.
This is an old book.

more.def: Having lived or existed for many years, or having a certain age.
examples: The old oak tree has stood in the park for over a hundred years.
My little brother is five years old.
She wore her old boots because the new ones hurt.
In olden times, people rode horses.
Those were the olden days.
Olden stories are told.

more.def: Belonging to a time long ago.
examples: In olden times, people traveled by horse.
Grandpa told stories about the olden days.
The olden castle stood on the hill.

easy.def: An old song or movie that people still like.
examples: That song is an oldie.
Grandpa plays oldies.
We danced to an oldie.

more.def: An old song, movie or show that people still enjoy.
examples: Grandpa loves to play oldies on his record player.
That song is an oldie but a goodie.
We danced to an oldie at the party.

easy.def: A small green or black fruit with a pit.
examples: I eat an olive.
The olive is salty.
Olives grow on trees.

more.def: A small green or black fruit with a pit, eaten whole or pressed to make oil.
examples: I ate an olive with my pizza.
Olive oil comes from olives.
Olives grow on trees in warm places.

easy.def: A big sports event held every four years.
examples: The Olympics are every four years.
We watched the Olympics.
She won a medal at the Olympics.

more.def: A sports contest held every four years, in which athletes from many countries compete.
examples: Athletes from all over the world come to the Olympics.
We watched the swimming races at the Olympics on TV.
The next Olympics will be held in a different city.
